Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production model latency spike in westus-2 — urgent

Jonas / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sustained latency and 5xx error increase against our embedding endpoint (model: rw-instruct-13b) in westus-2 starting ~08:40 PST. Error rate climbed to ~7% and p95 latency jumped from 120ms to 1.4s. This is causing timeouts in our ingestion pipeline and impacting customer-facing search.

Can you confirm whether this is localized to an AZ or a region? We need an ETA on mitigation — customers are already opening tickets. Please escalate to SRE and exec if needed.

Thanks,
Sarah

Subject: Re: Production model latency spike in westus-2 — urgent

Quick triage update (09:36 PST):
- Observed symptoms: sustained request queue growth on a subset of instances in AZ-A (westus-2). KV-cache warmup latency and provisioning lag spikes when autoscaler requests extra pods.
- Error mode: 502/504s from gateway timeouts when the backend queue depth exceeds threshold; routing and health checks still show region healthy overall, but several AZ-A hosts are overloaded.
- Root cause hypothesis: a combination of a model cold-start pattern after a recent scale event + an unexpected workload shape from Delta (batched ingestion bursts) causing concurrent provisioning thrash.

Recommendation (immediate):
1) Execute an emergency cross-region steer for Delta to eastus2 for 90 minutes (start now) to reduce p95 for their traffic.
2) While steer is active, pre-warm additional instance pool in westus-2 (one-time reserve) and increase per-host request queue limits carefully.
3) Post-event: run kernel-level profiling to see if quantized path is causing longer cold starts for this model.

Estimated trade-offs: temporary 8-12% higher per-token cost due to inter-region replication + ~10% added latency for some client calls depending on egress path.

I've attached a short timeline and the checklist for routing changes. Need green-light from leadership to authorize the traffic shift and the emergency pre-warm.

Attachment: p0-timeline.csv
Attachment: routing-change-checklist.pdf

-Dylan

Lauren — moving this to you for executive approval.

Requested approvals:
- Authorize emergency steering and allow the SRE team to run the pre-warm (estimated incremental cost: $3,200 for 12 hours).
- Authorize an immediate customer credit offer up to $6,000 if incident extends beyond 2 hours.

If we get verbal/GTM OK I will notify the customer and proceed. If Lauren is not reachable, Jonas you have discretionary approval up to $1,500; otherwise we need a rapid sign-off.

Marissa

Appreciate the fast triage. Two quick asks from our side:
1) ETA for the traffic reroute completion and an expected new p95 target
2) Clear rollback criteria (how we decide to move back to westus-2)

We need to communicate an ETA to our product and support teams (~10k MAU impacted). Also please include the impact on batch ingestion windows.

-Sarah
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Tallis <sarah.tallis@delta-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T17:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod latency/error surge in westus-2 — mitigation summary (actioned)

Quick closure note and timeline:
- 10:22 PST: emergency steer initiated for Delta traffic to eastus2.
- 10:30 PST: eastus2 routing confirmed; observed p95 drop from 1.4s -> 180ms for the majority of requests. Error rate back to ~0.3%.
- 10:45 PST: SRE started pre-warm in westus-2 and increased queue thresholds. No additional errors reported.
- 11:50 PST: began controlled gradual shift back for low-volume endpoints to test warm instances; full return to westus-2 scheduled pending RCA.

Actions next:
- SRE to produce RCA within 72 hours with kernel profiling and autoscaler tuning recommendations.
- Sales to coordinate customer credit and formal incident notification.
- Ops: run a replay of ingestion bursts in staging to validate pre-warm changes.

Links: postmortem draft: https://redwood.app/ops/bridges/bridge-20261118-jonas/postmortem
HubSpot: HS-7421

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. I'll keep the bridge open for the next hour for any remaining questions.
